newsitem.title: USA: Mideast group summit resumes amid differences.
newsitem.headline: Mideast group summit resumes amid differences.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday hosted the leaders of Israel, the Palestinians and Jordan for a top-level effort to overcome serious differences that threatened to stalemate his Middle East crisis summit.

"We're not there yet," a senior White House official said in reference to U.S. attempts to mediate Israeli-Palestinian agreement on issues that endanger the Middle East peace process. The official spoke after Secretary of State Warren Christopher concluded a negotiating session with Israeli and Palestinian deputies, and reports surfaced in Washington and Jerusalem that little or no progress had been made.

Clinton played host to a working lunch for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein. They were seated around a large table in the White House Blue Room with top aides.

Palestinian officials in Washington and Jerusalem said no agreements had been reached in Washington and that the Palestinians had rejected a series of Israeli demands. An Israeli official said his side had rejected a Palestinian demand for immediate troop withdrawals from the West Bank town of Hebron and countered with demands for security guarantees.
U.S. spokesmen, however, were less pessimistic in their assessments as the summit lunch began and suggested the two antagonists might be putting their own spin on matters for bargaining advantage.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry backed away from an earlier suggestion the summit might spill over into Thursday, saying the United States now "anticipated having a concluding session today."
